solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Full-length and unadulterated

definitions.meaning: a film or book not shortened by editing is shown in full
pure, with nothing mixed in or taken out

explanation.surface: Praise for a film or a spirit that comes complete and pure.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from not being trimmed: a complete edit of a film, and a drug or drink not diluted.

clue.text: Reach out and steal electronic device

parts.note: to push is to press outwards or extend, as a plant pushes out shoots
to pull is slang for carrying out a theft, as in pulling a job

explanation.surface: Someone stretches out a hand and pinches a gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A push-pull circuit is an amplifier arrangement in electronics using paired transistors or valves working alternately.

clue.text: Rang for special bargain

parts.note: truck is an old word meaning to barter or trade, as in 'have no truck with'

explanation.surface: Someone telephoned about a special offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell that is struck has rung; both are past forms describing a chime sounding out.

clue.text: Teacher's turning over carpet with a bit of underfelt

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the word for carpet is read backwards

parts.note: a rug is a small carpet

indicators.note: a bit of the word underfelt is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A teacher flips over the carpet to look at the underlay beneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' reverses RUG to GUR, and 'a bit of' takes the U that starts underfelt.
explanation.definitionFit: A guru is a spiritual instructor in Hinduism, and more widely any respected mentor.

clue.text: Place for head-covering? Around top of head

definitions.text: Place for head-covering? Around top of head

parts.words: Place for head-covering? Around top of head
parts.note: a cryptic description of a building where worshippers have traditionally covered their heads, the question mark flagging the playful angle

explanation.surface: A riddle about where a hat sits, round the crown of the head.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a hat on a head, but the place meant is a building where women traditionally wore hats or veils at services.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian custom long required women to cover their heads during worship in this building.

clue.text: Edits leaflet with indication of respect for American to create a foundation

parts.note: to sub is to subedit copy, so subs means edits

indicators.note: one thing standing for another signals a swap of one letter for another inside the leaflet

parts.note: a tract is a short pamphlet or leaflet
U is a Burmese honorific placed before a man's name, as in U Thant

explanation.surface: A subeditor tidies a pamphlet, adjusting a courtesy for American readers, to lay groundwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indication of respect' is U, the honorific Burmese men carry, as in U Thant; 'for' swaps it in where the A for American stood.
explanation.definitionFit: To substruct is to build underneath, so laying a base beneath a structure.

clue.text: Kind of whole food but not English

parts.note: whole can mean intact and uninjured

indicators.note: but not tells us to leave the following letter out of the previous word

parts.note: fuel is food in the sense of what keeps a body going

explanation.surface: Sounds like a description of a type of wholefood that isn't English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of whole food' reads as one phrase about wholefood; 'Kind' alone is the definition. 'but not English' takes E out of FUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that causes no hurt is gentle and considerate, a fair sense of kind.

clue.text: Quiet game with barrels for Bush

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
RU is Rugby Union, a game
b is a recognised abbreviation for barrels, as in measures of oil

explanation.surface: A quiet game played among barrels, standing in for a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bush and a shrub are the same thing: a woody plant smaller than a tree.

clue.text: Holy man spoke and got hanged

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for saint, a holy man
a rung is a spoke or crossbar, as of a chair or ladder

explanation.surface: A holy man spoke out and was executed for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoke' looks like the past of speak, but it is a noun: a crossbar, RUNG.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone strung up has been hanged, the phrase being informal for execution by rope.

clue.text: Shut up! That's bad language

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of the phrase are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone told to shut up protests that it is bad language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges the letters of SHUT UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushtu, also spelt Pashto, is the tongue of the Pashtun people of Afghanistan and Pakistan.

clue.text: Riding by way of street required for taking off vertically

parts.note: up means riding, as a jockey is said to be up on a horse
thru is the informal spelling of through, meaning by way of

explanation.surface: A rider travels down a street, needing a vertical take-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Upthrust is an upward push, the force that lifts something straight up off the ground.

clue.text: Disturbance caused by American following a mass of ordinary people

indicators.note: following puts the American piece after the crowd

parts.note: the ruck is the common crowd, the undistinguished mass
US stands for American, as in US forces

explanation.surface: A disturbance stirred up by an American who follows the common crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruckus is a noisy commotion or row, a North American informal word.

clue.text: To play with sweep on street with spirit

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: A chimney sweep plays about in the street with a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweep' sounds like a chimney sweep, but here it is the sweeping movement of a hand across guitar strings.
explanation.definitionFit: To strum is to sweep fingers or a plectrum across the strings of a guitar.

clue.text: Ben perhaps replaces one in military group not being injured

indicators.note: replaces says one piece takes the place of another inside the word

parts.note: a unit is a military group
I is the Roman numeral one
Ben-Hur is the hero of the novel and film, so the name that follows Ben there is Hur

explanation.surface: A soldier called Ben steps in for a comrade in the regiment who is not wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ben perhaps' points to Ben-Hur: Ben is followed by HUR, which 'replaces' the I in UNIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhurt means unharmed, describing someone who has come through without injury.

clue.text: Tipper put Mr Duck in trouble

indicators.note: something in trouble is in a mess, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone has landed a Mr Duck in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tipper' looks like a person who leaves tips; it is a lorry that tips its load.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipper is a lorry whose body tilts to unload, which is what this vehicle does.

clue.text: Body to throw right to left

indicators.note: right to left reads as changing the letter for right into the letter for left

parts.note: to hurl is to throw hard

explanation.surface: A body is thrown from right to left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right to left' looks like a direction of throw; it swaps R (right) for L (left) in HURL.
explanation.definitionFit: The hull is the main body of a ship or boat.

clue.text: Fiddles about around her heartless expression of doubt

indicators.note: around tells us the reversed fiddles word encloses what follows
about means turned round, so the fiddles word is read backwards

parts.note: a gu is a type of fiddle from Shetland, so gus are fiddles

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letter of her

explanation.surface: Someone fiddles about around a woman lacking feeling, and gets doubtful looks.
explanation.walkthrough: A gu is a Shetland fiddle, a word few solvers know; 'about' turns the plural round and 'heartless' drops the middle of her before it goes 'around'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting the shoulders is a gesture of doubt or indifference.

clue.text: At school stomach's quiet

parts.note: tum is the informal word for stomach

explanation.surface: A schoolchild's stomach goes quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Schtum is Yiddish-derived slang for silent, as in keeping your mouth shut.

clue.text: Friar's food

definitions.meaning: Friar ... is the jolly monk in the Robin Hood legends
British schoolchildren's slang for snacks and sweets

explanation.surface: What a monk eats.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuck is a British word for food, especially sweets bought at a school tuck shop.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the name of Robin Hood's monk; the other is slang for edible treats.

clue.text: Not lying in the full endless furrow

indicators.note: in tells us the furrow sits inside the trimmed words
endless cuts the last letter from each of the two words

parts.note: a rut is a furrow or groove

explanation.surface: Someone honest lies flat in a long furrow that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims THE and FULL to TH and FUL, giving THFUL; 'in' puts RUT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tells no lies is honest, speaking only the truth.

clue.text: A rising surge could be made of sulphur with no end of amatol

indicators.note: could be made of says the letters, less one, can be rebuilt into a new word
the end of amatol is its last letter

explanation.surface: An upward surge from an explosive mix of sulphur lacking its amatol.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove L, the last letter of amatol, from SULPHUR and rearrange the remaining SUPHUR. Amatol is a high explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: An uprush is an upward rush, a sudden surge that rises.

clue.text: Open local one's shed

parts.note: 'un is dialect for one, as in 'a good 'un', so the local one's is 'un's
a hut is a small shed

explanation.surface: A neighbour's shed has been left open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' signals the dialect form 'un for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Unshut is an old word for opened or not closed.

clue.text: Robin Goodfellow has hesitation, then changes ends to make a mess of things

indicators.note: changes ends tells us the first and last letters of the combination trade places

parts.note: Robin Goodfellow is another name for Puck, the mischievous sprite in A Midsummer Night's Dream
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A mischievous sprite hesitates, then switches sides and makes a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: PUCK plus UM gives PUCKUM; 'changes ends' swaps its first and last letters, P and M.
explanation.definitionFit: To muck up is informal for bungling or spoiling things.

clue.text: Show when usefulness initially replaced a bit of artistry in skilled trades

indicators.note: replaced tells us one letter has been put in the place of another inside the trades word

parts.note: crafts are skilled trades

indicators.note: a bit of artistry is its opening letter
initially picks the opening letter of usefulness

explanation.surface: A display of handiwork where practicality has won out over artistry.
explanation.walkthrough: CRUFTS is Britain's famous annual dog show. In CRAFTS, the A (first of artistry) is 'replaced' by U (first of usefulness).
explanation.definitionFit: Crufts is the large dog show held each year in Birmingham, England.

clue.text: This could sweep up pieces of 8

indicators.note: breaking something up into pieces signals that its letters are jumbled

parts.note: 8 refers to the answer at 8 across, a word for a bush

explanation.surface: A broom might sweep up bits of plant debris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up pieces of' breaks up the letters of the bush word at 8 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A broom-like tool with bristles is used for sweeping floors.

clue.text: Slices of cone become dull when smothered by fumes out East

indicators.note: smothered by means wrapped round, so the dulling word goes inside
out says a letter is put out of the word fumes

parts.note: to rust is to lose a shine and become dull

explanation.surface: Pieces of a cone grow tarnished when wreathed in fumes from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' drops the E for East from fumes, and 'smothered by' wraps what is left round the dulling word.
explanation.definitionFit: A frustum is the part of a cone or pyramid left after cutting off the top with a parallel plane.

clue.text: Fabric's acceptable for international mood

indicators.note: putting one thing in for another signals a letter swap within the fabric

parts.note: silk is a fabric
U means socially acceptable or upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A fabric suits an international mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps I (international) in SILK for U, the old label for upper-class and acceptable usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A sulk is a sullen, bad-tempered mood.

clue.text: Sulphur doesn't start to be thrown out by what a volcano does

indicators.note: thrown out suggests the remaining letters are tossed around into a new order
doesn't start drops the opening letter of sulphur

explanation.surface: Sulphur is ejected by an erupting volcano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't start' leaves ULPHUR, which 'thrown out' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To uphurl is to fling upwards, as an erupting crater does with ash and rock.

clue.text: Namely strange 12

parts.note: sc is the abbreviation for scilicet, Latin for namely
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A cryptic call that names something odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 points to the answer at 12 across, a disturbance; a scrum is a disorderly crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A disorderly crush of people struggling together is a melee or commotion.

clue.text: Black pudding in Black Forest

parts.note: the Black Forest is in Germany, so the clue asks for the German word for a blood sausage

explanation.surface: A blood sausage served in the Black Forest region.
explanation.walkthrough: Black pudding is a British blood sausage; 'in Black Forest' asks for the German name.
explanation.definitionFit: Blutwurst is the German blood sausage, the equivalent of black pudding.
